title: Example log fields
description: Structure and validation rules for a log entry emitted by software

timestamp.title: Timestamp
timestamp.description: The date and time at which the log entry was created, expressed in ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 format. The value MUST be in UTC and MUST include the 'Z' timezone designator or a '+00:00' offset. Sub-second precision (up to microseconds) is recommended.

level.title: Log Level
level.description:
The severity level of the log entry. Use the string identifier — never the numeric value. Levels mirror the Python standard logging library:
  DEBUG (10)    — Detailed diagnostics, useful only during development.
  INFO (20)     — Significant business or operational events (default level).
  WARNING (30)  — Unexpected situations that may indicate future problems.
  ERROR (40)    — Failures that affect a specific operation but not the whole program.
  CRITICAL (50) — Failures that affect the entire program or require immediate attention.

message.title: Message
message.description: A human-readable description of the event being logged. Messages should be specific, self-contained, and actionable. Include relevant identifiers and error details directly in the string rather than relying on other fields to provide context. Prefer 'Failed to save subject info: field experiment_id is missing' over 'Save failed'.
examples: Failed to save subject info: field 'experiment_id' is missing
Failed to save session: could not connect to database

examples.$comment: Sequence of minimal JSONL-style entries (each would be one line in a .jsonl file)
